result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is a full journey map: a named persona, does/asks/feels rows, and a 'touches us' row that links each stage to something the studio owns (website times, membership page, follow-up email, kiln schedule, shelves). It also labels its own guesses ('our inference', 'not raised'). A is clear and marks the bad moments well, but it doesn't track what the member thinks at each stage and only hints at what the studio owns, apart from the ideas section, which is cut off in the screenshot. B's grid is denser but still easy to read. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is a proper journey map. It names one persona, follows six stages in order, and has rows for what the member does, asks and feels, a 'touches us' row, and a 'goes wrong' row. The pain points and the trial-class high are colour-coded, and its counts stay within the six people interviewed. B is cleaner and very legible, with accurate counts and clearly marked pain points, but it shows less of what the member thinks and feels, and has no explicit row for what the studio owns (its 'ideas to discuss' section is cut off), so staff get less help seeing what to change.
